question: The distance between the centres of the two circles is 73 cm, and the radii of the circles are 29 cm and 19 cm. Find the length of the transverse common tangent drawn to the two circles.
solution:
"
 * *Wait, I've spent too much time checking constraints. I will proceed with the generation.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Length of **Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)** = √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²)

Sum of radii = 29 + 19 = 48 cm

TCT = √(73² − 48²)

Using a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b):

TCT = √((73 − 48) × (73 + 48)) = √(25 × 121) = 5 × 11 = 55 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 55 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between centres (d) = 73 cm

Radius of first circle (r₁) = 29 cm

Radius of second circle (r₂) = 19 cm

**Formula Used:**

Length of Transverse Common Tangent = √[(Distance between centres)² − (r₁ + r₂)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d72a5f644f40b8ef228bee937567c4926870e668bd105fcec6cd4f1c5e91900e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of radii = r₁ + r₂ = 29 + 19 = 48 cm

⇒ Length of TCT = √(73² − 48²)

⇒ Length of TCT = √(5329 − 2304)

⇒ Length of TCT = √3025

⇒ Length of TCT = 55 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 55 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of the direct common tangent is given by √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²).

Number of Common Tangents

If d > r₁ + r₂, there are 4 common tangents (2 direct, 2 transverse). If d = r₁ + r₂, there are 3 common tangents.

Pythagorean Triplet

The numbers (48, 55, 73) form a Pythagorean triplet since 48² + 55² = 2304 + 3025 = 5329 = 73².</p
